findings.title: Asked for in Jira but not mentioned in the code: AQPI-8 4.2 Sort and filter hotel results
findings.detail: 4 acceptance criteria of AQPI-8 (epic AQPI-6) have no implementation in the code: The guest can apply supported filters such as price range, amenities, hotel category, and distance when data is available. The guest can sort using approved options. Selected criteria are visible and removable. Zero results after filtering offer a reset option.
findings.suggestion: Exclude it from this cycle as a gap (a Minor gap defect is raised and the story is picked up again in the next release), or discuss with the developer and the product owner.

findings.title: Asked for in Jira but not mentioned in the code: AQPI-13 5.3 Explain and control personalization
findings.detail: 3 acceptance criteria of AQPI-13 (epic AQPI-10) have no implementation in the code: The interface identifies when offers are personalized where required. The guest can proceed without selecting ancillary products. A consent or preference change affects future eligible recommendations according to policy.
findings.suggestion: Exclude it from this cycle as a gap (a Minor gap defect is raised and the story is picked up again in the next release), or discuss with the developer and the product owner.

findings.title: Asked for in Jira but not mentioned in the code: AQPI-22 7.4 Show booking outcome
findings.detail: 3 acceptance criteria of AQPI-22 (epic AQPI-18) have no implementation in the code: Success displays confirmation identifier, hotel, stay summary, selected products, and total. A failure does not display a false confirmation. Unknown or timeout states instruct the guest not to resubmit blindly and provide a safe recovery path.
findings.suggestion: Exclude it from this cycle as a gap (a Minor gap defect is raised and the story is picked up again in the next release), or discuss with the developer and the product owner.

skills.name: Automation script conventions
skills.description: How every generated Playwright spec is shaped, named and asserted, so scripts stay reviewable and runnable cycle after cycle.

skills.name: Test cycle report
skills.description: The fixed shape of every cycle report, so two cycles can be read side by side without translation.

skills.name: Defect reporting
skills.description: What a defect must contain before it is raised, so every cycle's defects read the same and are actionable.

skills.name: Incremental load and merge rules
skills.description: How an addition is classified against the baseline and what a human must see before it merges.

skills.name: Input normalisation and provenance
skills.description: How several inputs become one requirement set, and what must be visible about where each statement came from.

skills.name: Input review before the human gate
skills.description: What the review agent checks in the project inputs and how it words its suggestions for the reviewer.

skills.name: Test case authoring and Zephyr export shape
skills.description: One house style for every test case, so each cycle exports into Zephyr the same way.

skills.name: Test data generation from the input specs
skills.description: Every test case gets a complete, spec-conformant data set built from the data dictionary in the codebase input.

skills.name: Functional testing
skills.description: Steers the design agents to cover every business rule and its boundaries through the service API.

skills.name: Traceability hand-over
skills.description: What each phase owes the next one so the chain from input to defect never breaks in any cycle.

rows.text: A guest can complete the complete search-to-confirmation flow using valid inputs.
Only bookable inventory and valid rates are presented as available.
Total price is disclosed before confirmation, including mandatory taxes and fees.
Ancillary offers do not block booking when declined or unavailable.
The platform prevents or safely handles duplicate reservation submissions.
A successful reservation produces a durable confirmation identifier.
Confirmation is displayed on screen and an email request is generated.
Required business and technical events are logged using approved identifiers and masking rules.
All child user stories meet their acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done.
Negative and error paths for each story are tested and evidenced.
Required logging is in place and verified free of sensitive data.
The Product Owner has accepted the capability end to end.
Given valid search criteria, when the guest submits the search, then a search request is created and matching available hotels are returned.
The submitted criteria remain visible and editable on the results page.
Past check-in dates, check-out dates not after check-in, and missing mandatory fields are rejected with actionable messages.
A no-availability result explains that no matching inventory was found and allows criteria changes.
Check-in must precede check-out.
Occupancy must comply with configured room limits.
Maximum stay length must be configurable.
Required fields are clearly identified.
Invalid combinations return field-level messages.
Server validation is authoritative when client and server results differ.
Validation messages are accessible to assistive technology.
Validation rules must be configurable where market or property rules vary.
Zero results provide options to alter dates, occupancy, destination, or filters.
Technical failures display a non-technical message and retry option.
Repeated submission does not create inconsistent sessions.
Each result shows hotel name, location, representative image, starting price, currency, and availability indicator.
Mandatory fees or pricing qualifications are clearly disclosed.
Unavailable hotels are not presented as immediately bookable.
Results support pagination or progressive loading.
Displayed starting price must correspond to a valid rate returned for the search criteria.
Hotel description, images, location, amenities, room options, pricing, major policies, and relevant restrictions are displayed.
The guest can select a valid room and rate plan.
If inventory changes, the guest is informed before continuing.
Rate conditions and cancellation terms must be shown before selection.
The service considers available context such as stay dates, season, destination, hotel, room, party composition, declared interests, and consented profile attributes.
Unavailable or ineligible products are excluded.
The service returns a reason code for each recommended item.
When personalization data is unavailable, safe contextual defaults may be returned.
Sensitive traits must not be inferred or used.
Personalization must honor consent and data-retention rules.
Business rules and model versions must be auditable.
Each offer shows name, description, price, currency, applicability, and any restrictions.
The guest can add, skip, or dismiss an offer.
Offers are clearly distinguished from mandatory fees.
Failure to load offers does not block room booking.
The cart contains hotel, room, rate plan, stay dates, occupancy, quantity, currency, and price components.
Inventory and price are revalidated when required.
The cart has a defined expiration and displays relevant timeout behavior.
A cart must not itself create a reservation.
Price-change handling must require guest acknowledgement when material.
The guest can add an available ancillary.
Supported quantities can be changed within product limits.
Removal updates totals immediately.
Ineligible or sold-out products cannot be retained silently.
Room charges, taxes, mandatory fees, optional products, discounts, and total are itemized.
Currency is consistently displayed.
Material changes are highlighted and require acknowledgement.
The guest can return to edit supported selections.
The final payable total must be revalidated before reservation submission.
Required and optional fields are clearly distinguished.
Inputs are validated and error messages are accessible.
The guest receives applicable privacy notice and consent controls.
Data is transmitted securely and is not exposed in client logs.
Data minimization applies.
Sensitive values must be masked in support tools and excluded from analytics logs.
The guest sees the final payable or guarantee amount before authorization.
Payment data is handled through approved secure components.
Authorization success, decline, timeout, and technical failure are handled distinctly.
The product does not store prohibited card data in application logs.
Payment requirements depend on rate conditions.
Retry behavior must avoid duplicate authorization.
A successful request creates one reservation and returns a confirmation identifier.
Repeated submissions with the same idempotency key do not create duplicate reservations.
Inventory, price, payment, and reservation outcomes remain reconcilable.
Partial failures trigger defined recovery or manual-review handling.
Reservation submission must use an idempotency mechanism.
The source of truth for confirmation status must be defined.
The message contains guest-safe confirmation details, hotel information, stay dates, booked items, pricing summary, and applicable policy information.
The message content matches the confirmed reservation state.
Templates support required locale and accessibility standards.
Only necessary personal data may be included.
Sensitive payment details must not appear.
A successful reservation creates one confirmation-email request.
Send failure does not reverse a valid reservation.
Permitted retries avoid duplicate or excessive messages.
Operational users can distinguish queued, sent, delivered, bounced, and failed states when supported by the provider.
Email addresses must be masked outside authorized operational views.
The request verifies sufficient reservation information without exposing data.
Rate limits and abuse controls apply.
The resend creates a new message event without creating a new reservation.
Sensitive data is classified and mapped to approved storage and processing locations.
Data is encrypted in transit and at rest where required.
Logs and analytics exclude or mask prohibited fields.
Access to operational data is role-based and auditable.
Retention and deletion follow approved policy.
Events use a correlation ID across supported services.
Business events and technical logs are distinguishable.
Metrics and alerts exist for agreed critical failures and latency.
Logging degradation does not expose sensitive payloads or silently block booking unless explicitly required.
Event schemas must be versioned.
Production log access must be controlled and retained according to policy.
Keyboard navigation, focus order, labels, instructions, status messaging, and error handling are accessible.
Visual information is not conveyed by color alone.
Dynamic updates are announced appropriately.
Email templates are readable and structurally accessible.
Search, pricing, cart, checkout, reservation, and email dependencies have agreed performance targets.
Timeout, retry, circuit-breaker, and fallback behavior are documented.
Load, resilience, and recovery tests cover critical journeys.
Reservation integrity is prioritized over non-critical personalization and analytics.
A cart expires 30 minutes after it is created and never creates a reservation itself.
A price change of more than 1% must be acknowledged by the guest before checkout.
A confirmation can be resent at most 3 times per booking in 24 hours.
Every reservation request needs an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 64 characters; a replay within 24 hours returns the original outcome.
A stay can be at most 30 nights; Paris (PAR) allows at most 21 nights.
Each room holds at most 4 adults and 3 children, and one search books 1 to 8 rooms.
Check-in can be at most 500 days ahead.

rows.description: Destination code the guest searches (demo catalogue: New York, London, Paris)
Check-in date as days from today (0 = today)
Nights between check-in and check-out (PAR allows at most 21)
Adults in the party (at least one per room, at most 4 per room)
Children in the party (at most 3 per room)
Room type chosen on the hotel details page
FLEX = pay at hotel with a card guarantee; SAVER = prepaid, non-refundable
Optional ancillary added to the cart (empty = none)
Token from the secure payment component; raw card numbers are never accepted
Prefix of the Idempotency-Key sent with a reservation (the full key is 8 to 64 characters)

narrative.text: Hotel booking baseline · Functional (baseline) worked from Jira initiative AQPI-1 (Jira export on GitHub), Jira epic AQPI-2, AQPI-6, AQPI-10, AQPI-14, AQPI-18, AQPI-23, AQPI-27 (Jira export on GitHub), Codebase sri465inno/uc-agentic-quality-engineering@demo/hotel-booking-platform (b212a32) (pulled live from GitHub). The reviewed requirement set holds 118 requirements. 121 test cases are designed, 65 of them automated in 50 Playwright scripts. Execution ran 65 automated cases for real: 62 passed and 3 failed (pass rate 95.4%). 6 defect(s) were raised from real failures: DEF-004 AQPI-8 4.2 Sort and filter hotel results: asked for in Jira but not implemented in the code; DEF-005 AQPI-13 5.3 Explain and control personalization: asked for in Jira but not implemented in the code; DEF-006 AQPI-22 7.4 Show booking outcome: asked for in Jira but not implemented in the code; DEF-007 A price change within 1% does not need acknowledgement: returns true instead of false; DEF-008 A key shorter than 8 characters is refused: returns 201 instead of 400; DEF-009 9 rooms in one search are rejected: returns 200 instead of 400.
